deck_title: Euler Elastica inextensible bending vs naive transverse shear stretching rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Leonhard Euler (1744, Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas) inextensible Elastica bending law ((dx/ds, dy/ds) = (cos(theta(s)), sin(theta(s))), retracting the axial height coordinate as cos(theta) = 1/(1+u) when the strand bends by angle theta so total arc length L = int sqrt(cos^2(theta) + sin^2(theta)) ds locks at L/L_0 = 1.0000x across all 17 bending stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 stretched stations) versus naive linear transverse-only vertex shear (pos.x += windOffset * s while keeping pos.y = s fixed, which stretches hypotenuse arc length as sec(theta) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at theta=60 deg u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-segment Kirchhoff rod arc-length quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Real-time GPU grass blades, wheat fields, bamboo stalks, hair strands, and fur bending under strong wind
Cantilever fishing rods, radio whips, and robotic continuum arms requiring exact rest-length preservation
Retracting vertical coordinate y = s * cos(theta) alongside horizontal sway x = s * sin(theta) (or circular arc sin(k*s)/k, (1-cos(k*s))/k)
Eliminating the 2x rubber-band growth artifact when grass blades bend to 60 degrees
not_for: Highly extensible rubber bungee cords that are physically intended to stretch to 2x-3x their rest length
Rigid stone walls with zero bending deflection
